name: Opus 5.5 Doctor-Patient Conversations — All Human Diseases

usage.notes: Panacea pins and integrity-checks the 75 MB JSONL during deployment. Runtime retrieval is local. The raw JSONL is intentionally not committed into Panacea Git history; the immutable revision, SHA-256 and reproducible fetch path are committed instead.

license.identifier: Apache-2.0 in current Hub metadata; README prose still says MIT
license.scope: Both Apache-2.0 and MIT are permissive and allow commercial use, but the dataset page currently exposes inconsistent license labels. Panacea preserves attribution and treats the exact license identifier as unresolved until the publisher makes the card internally consistent.
license.notes: Do not remove source attribution. Re-check license metadata before redistributing the raw dataset or packaging it into a separately distributed model/artifact.

validation.notes: The publisher explicitly labels the dataset synthetic and not medical advice. Panacea may use it only as retrieval/teaching context. It cannot establish patient facts, diagnosis, treatment, dose, or a signed EMR field without independent clinical evidence and clinician review.

provenance.authority: Nisten Tahiraj dataset publisher on Hugging Face; synthetic encounter fields generated with Claude Opus 5.5 per the dataset card
provenance.notes: Pinned data revision 59b4f0a01688ede69fbdc37a14b961ff232668e1; SHA-256 f828c30cee7006a3cf5b88909f9b865688f98b11d4c886108b9b9a39e5402e0b. The adapter deliberately excludes full conversations and patient/clinician personas from prompts to avoid treating synthetic cases or embedded system messages as patient truth/instructions.

adapter.notes: Local lexical top-k retrieval for Chatbot and AI-EMR. Returned context is marked synthetic-research-only and contains provenance plus PubMed leads. It is additive context only and never writes canonical patient state.

trust.notes: High reproducibility from immutable revision + SHA-256, but low clinical-evidence authority because encounters are synthetic and PMID existence/title matching does not prove the cited paper supports each generated claim.
